reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
September Wednesdays used to be the hardest days for me to drink through. Not Friday night — Friday had a shape, a permission built into it. Wednesday was just Wednesday. Nothing to celebrate, nothing to numb, and yet there I was, three deep by 7 p.m., because I didn't know what to do with a plain evening. The middle of the week was a mirror I didn't want to look into.

The surprise of getting sober wasn't the big moments — it was learning that a plain Wednesday could be enough. That coming home, making dinner, calling someone back, reading twenty pages before bed — this wasn't a lesser life. This was the actual thing. The years I spent chasing intensity had trained me to mistake noise for meaning. Sobriety quieted the noise, and underneath it was a life I could actually feel.

Durant's line, riffing on Aristotle, gets at something I only understood years in: you don't become someone new in one heroic decision. You become someone new by what you do on the days no one is watching. The Wednesday you show up for yourself — the meeting you go to, the walk you take, the drink you don't pour — that's the person you're becoming. Not the highlight reel. The reps.
reflection.meditation: What would it mean to treat today as the day that counts, not the one you're getting through to reach something better?

affirmations: I am building a life through what I do on ordinary days, not just the big ones.
Today I have the agency to choose my next action, no matter what came before it.
I can sit with a quiet evening without needing to escape it.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Wednesday I can remember. Grateful for the small mechanics of a sober life — the coffee, the walk, the honest conversation, the clear head at bedtime. Grateful that the people who love me get the real version now, not the one I used to send in my place. And grateful for whoever kept showing up long enough to teach me that ordinary is its own kind of gift.
gratitude.closing: One more day, on its own terms. That's the whole thing.
